newsitem.title: USA: Akorn expects to break even for 1996 Q4. [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Akorn expects to break even for 1996 Q4. [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT]

text.p: Akorn Inc said Wednesday it expects to break even for the 1996 fourth quarter. It earned $296,000, or $0.02 a share, in the year-earlier period.
The company also said it expects to break even for the 1996 second half. A year earlier it earned $795,000, or $0.05 a share.
As previously announced, Akorn has changed its fiscal year-end to December 31 from June 30, creating a six-month "stub" period.

The company said it plans to relocate its ophthalmic division from Abita Springs to Chicago this year. As a result, it expects to incur severance and relocation expenses and a write-down of the Louisiana facility that will result in a first-quarter charge of $850,000 to $950,000 (corrects from $850,000 to $900,000) after taxes, it said.

Akorn said it will also change the timing of overhead absorption in its manufacturing operations, resulting in an additional first-quarter charge of $250,000 to $350,000 (corrects from $250,000 to $300,000) after taxes.
Akorn said it did not expect these changes to affect compliance with its loan covenants.
